name: Nestor Makhno
role: Ukrainian anarchist insurgent commander and exile writer
summary: Makhno advocated a stateless communist society administered by workers and peasants through free councils and federations. He combined opposition to party dictatorship with support for disciplined, voluntary revolutionary armies; wartime policies also imposed coercive penalties on counterrevolutionaries.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He supported abolishing state armies but explicitly advocated a coordinated revolutionary army for defense.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: His ABC says libertarian communists have no need of prisons, executioners or spies and tells people to disarm police and tear down the prisons; as a delegate in 1917 he demanded the militia's abolition.

class-collaboration.rationale: The platform insists on class struggle against capitalist masters rather than partnership.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The platform identifies class struggle as the primary determinant of historical social structures.

clerical-rule.rationale: He lists the priest among the five pillars of the state to be eliminated and says the state and its priests keep people in servitude.

collective-farming.rationale: The Platform commits anarchists to propaganda for collective agriculture, but leaves the final form (communal or family) to the peasants themselves, with no outside pressure.

confederal-coordination.rationale: He pictures free affinity groups linking into federations and confederations in a decentralised society, though the Platform also gives the Union an executive committee.

conscription.rationale: He condemns the Red Army being recruited by force and the Platform bases revolutionary forces on voluntary service, but Avrich reports that his own congress's "voluntary mobilization" worked as conscription.

cooperative-communities.rationale: It advocates collective agrarian organization within a federation of self-governing producers.

death-penalty.rationale: His ABC says libertarian communists have no need of executioners, yet he had pogromists and looters shot and his army's declaration ordered counter-revolutionaries shot.

decide-locally.rationale: The platform rejects centralism and defends independent initiative through voluntary federation.

defend-planned-state.rationale: His 1931 text urges revolutionary destruction of the Bolshevik order, rather than defense of its claimed proletarian character.

democracy-best.rationale: The Platform has a section on the negation of democracy, calling it a form of bourgeois dictatorship in which parliament and representative government serve the owning class.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: He rejects a "proletarian" state dictatorship as a new ruling class, but the Platform and his army's declaration deny non-working classes any share in power or soviets.

direct-action.rationale: He praises peasants' direct revolutionary seizure of the land before October, sees May Day as a rally to weigh direct armed struggle, and blames the Spanish revolution's ballot-box origin for its failure.

distribute-by-need.rationale: It explicitly makes need, rather than wealth or work performed, the basis of distribution.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He says science has shown God does not exist and divine ordinances on earth are artificial, so political authority has no divine source.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He defends the idea of equality against the Bolshevik congress that treated it as intolerable and attacks pay privileges for party members, and the Platform shares products on an equal basis.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: He tells the oppressed to banish all power from within them and to allow none over them, and says there is no such thing as harmless power, even for a power presented as workers'.

gradual-change.rationale: The platform rejects transitional regimes and demands immediate abolition of the state.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: The Platform allows no non-working classes and would admit former owners only on the same terms as other workers.

independent-unions.rationale: His army’s declaration protects workers’ unions and excludes political-party representatives from their governing councils.

informal-organisation.rationale: He campaigns for a permanent, disciplined federation of anarchists and tells Malatesta that rejecting collective responsibility endangers the revolution.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The Platform states that labour, physical or intellectual, is the only creator of social value and that only labour has a right to manage economic life.

land-redistribution.rationale: He organized expropriation and redistribution of landed estates to peasants.

land-use-tenure.rationale: The platform assigns land to working peasants without rights to sell or rent it.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He calls divine ordinances artificial and wants written laws burned, so scripture cannot ground his law.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He calls on the oppressed to rise against all state power and treats tsars among the rulers who exploit the people.

national-self-determination.rationale: He says self-determination up to a break with Russia emerged naturally among Ukraine's peoples, but argues that an independent Ukrainian state would be worth no more to the toilers than any other.

natural-rulers.rationale: He holds that everyone is naturally anarchist and that rule was created by drones to exploit those who produce.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He endorses armed defense against counterrevolutionary armies.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: He tells his readers to tear up and burn the laws of the governors and holds that a healthy life is not built on written laws and power.

one-party-rule.rationale: It rejects dictatorship by any party as incompatible with workers’ freedom.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He insists workers themselves determine their social institutions and direct economic life.

party-commands-army.rationale: The Platform puts the revolutionary army wholly under the workers' and peasants' organisations, and he condemns any party's power over the workers.

party-controls-media.rationale: He demands free speech and press for workers, peasants, anarchists and Left SRs as the Kronstadt demands he commemorates, and his army's declaration called press freedom inalienable.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He wants an anarchist union built on collective discipline and responsibility, whether or not it calls itself a party, and the Platform binds members to carry out decisions once taken.

people-in-arms.rationale: The Platform arms all workers and peasants at first and bases the army on voluntary service under peasant and worker organisations, and his army's declaration abolished standing armies in favour of local self-defence.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: His ABC calls governments of right and left drones and exploiters who live on the people's labour, and he details the Bolsheviks' rapacity and privileges.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He supports Ukrainians’ rights to their language, culture and customs while rejecting chauvinist statehood.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: The Platform says formal freedoms of speech, press and association are tolerated only while they do not challenge the owning class, which controls the whole press and education.

production-for-use.rationale: The Platform makes the satisfaction of everyone's necessities of life the first task of the revolutionary economy, in production owned in common with no entrepreneur.

profit-exploitation.rationale: It describes propertied classes’ appropriation of workers’ products as exploitation.

property-fundamental.rationale: The platform demands expropriation of the bourgeoisie’s productive property.

public-ownership.rationale: It places the industrial means of production in common ownership of the working class.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He calls the divine ordinances behind earthly rulers artificial and rejects earthly gods and every ruling power over others.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: He states that science has demonstrated the nonexistence of God, the supposed author of scripture.

smash-state-machine.rationale: He advocates destroying state institutions rather than capturing them for another ruling party.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: He rejects the Soviet claim to workers’ power because the party rules over voiceless laborers.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He describes the new state as combining private and state capitalist interests against workers.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: He advocates independently organized revolutionary workers’ armed forces against state armies.

state-class-instrument.rationale: His coauthored platform describes the state as organized class violence against workers.

state-harmful.rationale: He calls for the state’s complete eradication and replacement by free councils.

strong-leader.rationale: He rejects any power over others, including a revolutionary or workers' power that replaces the bourgeois one.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Workers’ organizational freedoms coexisted with execution threats against counterrevolutionaries; his later writing condemns Bolshevik repression.

total-state.rationale: He wants all state power abolished and rejects any state directing economic and spiritual life, which the Bolsheviks pursued.

unions-good.rationale: The platform endorses revolutionary unions as vehicles for organized workers’ struggle.

vanguard-party.rationale: The Platform holds that the masses' anarchist tendencies stay dispersed without an organised anarchist collective as the revolution's theoretical driving force, and calls the Union the organised vanguard.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: The Platform argues that the bourgeoisie's monopoly of economic life gives it unlimited political power and makes democratic liberties merely nominal.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The Platform warns that private farming leads to commerce, accumulation, private property and the return of capital, so it opposes spreading property among small owners.

worker-ownership.rationale: The platform assigns production to all workers collectively, excluding private and state-appointed owners.

workers-councils.rationale: He identifies free workers’ councils as the basis of post-state self-direction.

workers-nation.rationale: He distinguishes workers’ emancipation from nationalist state-building and encourages international revolutionary solidarity.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Production is administered by elected organs continually controlled by the working masses.

notes:
Reviewed early union organizing and estate redistribution, civil-war administration and violence, national and Jewish questions, and mature exile writings through 1931–1933. Downloaded the full Struggle Against the State collection and all substantive Platform sections, plus Malet’s scholarly book, and searched them across the statement themes. Platform positions are coauthored positions he expressly defended in his own essays, not views assigned from an anarchist label. Army declarations receive medium confidence for his institutional record; their promises and coercive exceptions are both retained, with mixed answers low. His denunciations of antisemitism were checked against Malet, but do not automatically answer specific segregation, boycott or intermarriage laws. Culture and language support is distinguished from support for a Ukrainian nation-state. No specific modern ecology, technology or globalism policy was located; support for agricultural machinery does not mean technology solves most human problems. General equality does not answer specific gender, sexuality or reproductive-rights statements. No inference from atheism, military innovation or his wife’s educational work. Remaining nulls reviewed against all 490 statements. No inferred answers. Auditor identification: the runtime identifies this assistant as GPT-6/Codex but does not expose an exact version or variant; gpt-6 is the available identifier, not an asserted variant.

Merged with an independent claude-sonnet-5-5 audit: 34 answers taken from it, 28 agreed, 2 conflicts settled by the integrator.

claude-sonnet-5-5 notes: Independent second pass. Read in full: all 18 essays of The Struggle Against the State (earlier pass leaned on chapters 3, 4, 6, 10, 11 and 16), memoir vol. 1, My Visit to the Kremlin, the Platform sections, the Malatesta letter, the 1933 Rogdaev report and the 1920 army declaration, plus Avrich. Anti-state answers (monarchy, sacred ruler, strong leader, total state, clerical rule, scripture) rest on his stated rejection of all state power and of God, not on the anarchist label. Record over words: his army used conscription-like mobilization, executed pogromists and counter-revolutionaries and barred parties from soviets, so conscription, suppression of opposition and the death penalty are 0 low. Army declarations are counted at medium or low only. No Inferred answers. Blocked: the later memoir volumes (Under the Blows of the Counterrevolution) were not found as full English text on theanarchistlibrary.org; vol. 1 and the Kremlin chapters were used instead. Not searched: Alex Jones corpus (no appearance).
